title: Aqeedah
sub: Learn about Allah, His Messengers ﷺ and the Last Day

lessons.title: Why we learn belief
lessons.about: Why every Muslim must know what is necessary, impossible and possible for Allah.

cards.x: Every Muslim who has reached adulthood and is sane must know what is necessary for Allah, what is impossible for Him, and what is possible for Him. The same applies to the Messengers عليهم السلام.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, opening: the three judgements

cards.x: Something is necessary if the mind cannot picture it not being there. It is impossible if the mind cannot picture it existing. It is possible if the mind can picture it existing or not existing.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, opening: the three judgements

cards.x: Knowing these things protects your belief from doubt. You don't need to be a scholar: you need to know them clearly and be sure of them.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, opening: the three judgements

checks.q: Who must know what is necessary, impossible and possible for Allah?
checks.why: Umm al-Barahin makes this knowledge a duty on every Muslim who is sane and has reached adulthood, not only on scholars.
checks.src: Umm al-Barahin, opening: the three judgements

checks.q: Something the mind cannot picture not existing is called…
checks.why: If the mind cannot picture something not being there, it is necessary.
checks.src: Umm al-Barahin, opening: the three judgements

checks.q: Something the mind can picture existing or not existing is called…
checks.why: Something that can be pictured existing or not existing is possible, like anything in creation.
checks.src: Umm al-Barahin, opening: the three judgements

lessons.title: How we know Allah exists
lessons.about: Imam al-Sanusi's proof from the world around us.

cards.x: Everything in the world moves, rests, grows and fades. Things that are always changing are things that came into being.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, proof of His existence

cards.x: What came into being cannot bring itself into being. So the world needs a Maker who did not come into being: Allah.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, proof of His existence

cards.x: Imam al-Sanusi رحمه الله gives a proof for every attribute he mentions, so that the believer holds each one with understanding.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the proofs of the attributes

checks.q: Why does the world need a Maker?
checks.a: Because it came into being and cannot bring itself into being
checks.why: Something that came into being after not existing needs someone to bring it into being. That is Allah, who never came into being.

checks.q: What shows the world came into being?
checks.why: Al-Sanusi points to the constant change in the world: movement, rest, coming and going. What changes like this came into being.

checks.q: Can the Maker of the world have come into being too?
checks.a: No, otherwise He would need a maker as well
w: Yes, at the same time as the world
checks.why: If the Maker had come into being He would need a maker too, which never ends. So He has no beginning.

lessons.title: Allah exists, without beginning or end
lessons.about: Allah exists, with no beginning and no end, depending on nothing.

cards.x: Allah exists. His existence has no cause and does not depend on anything.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the necessary attributes

cards.x: Allah has no beginning (qidam). Everything else came into being after not existing; He did not.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the necessary attributes

cards.x: Allah has no end (baqa'). He will never cease to be. As Imam al-Tahawi رحمه الله says: He is Eternal without a beginning and Everlasting without an end.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on Allah's Oneness

checks.q: What does it mean that Allah has no beginning?
checks.a: He never came into being; He always was
w: He was created before everything else
He began when the universe began
No one knows if He has a beginning
checks.why: Qidam means Allah never came into being. Everything else existed after not existing; He did not.
checks.src: Umm al-Barahin, the necessary attributes · al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on Allah's Oneness

checks.q: What does it mean that Allah has no end?
checks.a: He will never cease to exist
w: He will end after the Last Day
He ends when the world ends
checks.why: Baqa' means Allah will never cease to be. Al-Tahawi calls Him Everlasting without an end.
checks.src: Umm al-Barahin, the necessary attributes · al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on Allah's Oneness

checks.q: Does Allah's existence depend on anything?
checks.why: Allah's existence has no cause and depends on nothing. Everything else depends on Him.
checks.src: Umm al-Barahin, the necessary attributes · al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on Allah's Oneness

lessons.title: Allah is unlike anything
lessons.about: Allah does not resemble His creation, needs nothing, and is One.

cards.x: Allah does not resemble anything He created. He is not a body, He is not in a place, and He is not bound by time. 'There is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.' (al-Shura 11)
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the necessary attributes

cards.x: Allah stands by Himself (qiyam bi-nafsihi): He needs no place and no one to bring Him into being. Everything needs Him.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the necessary attributes

cards.x: Allah is One (wahdaniyyah): One in His Self, One in His attributes and One in His actions. He has no partner and no equal.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the necessary attributes

checks.q: Which is true about Allah?
checks.a: He does not resemble anything He created
w: He has a body unlike ours
He is in one particular place
He is bound by time like us
checks.why: Allah is not a body, not in a place and not bound by time. 'There is nothing like Him.' (al-Shura 11)

checks.q: What does it mean that Allah 'stands by Himself'?
checks.a: He needs nothing, while everything needs Him
w: He needs His throne to exist
checks.why: Qiyam bi-nafsihi: Allah needs no place and no one to bring Him into being, while everything needs Him.

checks.q: Allah's Oneness covers…
checks.a: His Self, His attributes and His actions
checks.why: Wahdaniyyah covers all three: He is One in His Self, His attributes and His actions.

lessons.title: Seven attributes of Allah
lessons.about: Power, will, knowledge, life, hearing, sight and speech.

cards.x: Allah has Power (qudrah) over every possible thing, and Will (iradah): nothing happens except what He wills.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the attributes of meaning

cards.x: Allah has Knowledge ('ilm) of everything: what was, what is, what will be, and what would be. He is Living (hayah) with a life unlike ours.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the attributes of meaning

cards.x: Allah hears (sam') and sees (basar) all that exists, without ears or eyes. He speaks (kalam) with an eternal speech that is not letters or sounds. The Qur'an is His speech.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the attributes of meaning

checks.q: Nothing happens in creation except…
checks.why: Allah has Will (iradah): nothing happens in creation except what He wills.
checks.src: Umm al-Barahin, the attributes of meaning

checks.q: How does Allah hear and see?
checks.a: Without ears or eyes, unlike creation
w: With ears and eyes like ours
He does not hear or see
checks.why: Allah hears and sees all that exists without ears or eyes. His attributes are unlike ours.
checks.src: Umm al-Barahin, the attributes of meaning

checks.q: Allah's speech is…
checks.a: Eternal, and not made of letters or sounds
w: Something that began with the Qur'an
checks.why: Allah's speech is eternal and is not letters or sounds. The Qur'an is His speech.
checks.src: Umm al-Barahin, the attributes of meaning

lessons.title: The Speech of Allah
lessons.about: The Qur'an is Allah's speech, not created like ours.

cards.x: Allah speaks with an eternal speech. The Qur'an is the speech of Allah: it came from Him, without asking how, and He sent it down to His Messenger ﷺ as revelation.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on the Qur'an

cards.x: The believers are certain it is truly Allah's speech, not created like the speech of creation. Whoever hears it and claims it is human speech has disbelieved.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on the Qur'an

cards.x: Imam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله said: the Qur'an is written in the copies, preserved in the hearts and recited by the tongues. Our pronouncing, writing and reciting it are created; the Qur'an itself is not created.
cards.src: al-Fiqh al-Akbar, on the Qur'an

checks.q: What is the Qur'an?
checks.a: The speech of Allah, not created
w: The words of the Prophet ﷺ
A book written by the Companions
checks.why: Al-Tahawi: the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, from Him it came, not created like the speech of creation.

checks.q: According to Imam Abu Hanifah, which of these is created?
checks.why: Our pronouncing, writing and reciting are created. The Qur'an, Allah's speech, is not.

checks.q: Where is the Qur'an, according to al-Fiqh al-Akbar?
checks.a: Written in the copies, preserved in hearts, recited by tongues
checks.why: Abu Hanifah described it in all three ways: written, preserved in hearts and recited by tongues.

lessons.title: What is impossible and possible for Allah
lessons.about: The opposites of His attributes, and what He freely does.

cards.x: The opposite of every necessary attribute is impossible for Allah: non-existence, having a beginning or end, resembling creation, needing anything, having a partner, weakness, ignorance, death and so on.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, what is impossible for Allah

cards.x: What is possible for Allah is doing or leaving anything that is possible. Nothing obliges Him: if He rewards us it is pure bounty, and if He punishes it is pure justice.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, what is possible for Allah; Jawharat al-Tawhid

cards.x: This protects you from two mistakes: thinking Allah is like us, and thinking anything is forced upon Him.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, what is possible for Allah

checks.q: Which is impossible for Allah?
checks.why: Needing is the opposite of qiyam bi-nafsihi (standing by Himself), so it is impossible for Allah.

checks.q: What is possible for Allah?
w: Only what is best for creation
checks.why: Al-Sanusi: what is possible for Allah is doing or leaving any possible thing.

checks.q: Is Allah obliged to reward anyone?
checks.a: No, His reward is from His bounty
checks.why: Nothing is obligatory upon Allah. Al-Laqqani: if He rewards us it is pure bounty.

lessons.title: The Messengers عليهم السلام
lessons.about: What is necessary, impossible and possible for the Messengers.

cards.x: The Messengers are truthful (sidq), trustworthy (amanah) and convey everything they were commanded to convey (tabligh).
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, on the Messengers

cards.x: Lying, betraying trust, and hiding what they were commanded to convey are impossible for them.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, on the Messengers

cards.x: Human things that do not lower their rank are possible for them, such as eating, sleeping, marriage and illness that is not repulsive.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, on the Messengers

cards.x: Muhammad ﷺ is the last Prophet and the Messenger to all of mankind and jinn. There is no prophet after him.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on the Prophet ﷺ

checks.q: Which is necessary for every Messenger?
checks.a: Truthfulness, trustworthiness and conveying the message
checks.why: Truthfulness (sidq), trustworthiness (amanah) and conveying the message (tabligh) are necessary for every Messenger.
checks.src: Umm al-Barahin, on the Messengers · al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on the Prophet ﷺ

checks.q: Which is possible for a Messenger?
checks.why: Human things that do not lower their rank, such as eating, sleeping and marriage, are possible for them.
checks.src: Umm al-Barahin, on the Messengers · al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on the Prophet ﷺ

checks.q: Who is the last Prophet?
w: There will be another after him
checks.why: Muhammad ﷺ is the Seal: the last Prophet, with no prophet after him.
checks.src: Umm al-Barahin, on the Messengers · al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on the Prophet ﷺ

lessons.title: The meaning of the Shahadah
lessons.about: How 'la ilaha illa Allah' gathers all of belief.

cards.x: Imam al-Sanusi ends by showing that all of belief is gathered in 'La ilaha illa Allah, Muhammadun Rasulullah'.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the meaning of the Shahadah

cards.x: Its meaning: there is none who is free of need of everything else, and whom everything else needs, except Allah. Every attribute we learnt follows from this.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the meaning of the Shahadah

cards.x: 'Muhammadun Rasulullah' brings in belief in all the Prophets and angels, the books and the Last Day, because he ﷺ came with all of it. So say it often, knowing what it means.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the meaning of the Shahadah

checks.q: What does 'la ilaha illa Allah' mean, according to al-Sanusi?
checks.a: None is free of need of all else, and needed by all, except Allah
w: There are many gods but Allah is the best
checks.why: Al-Sanusi explains it as: none is free of need of everything else and needed by everything else except Allah.

checks.q: Belief in the angels and the Last Day is contained in…
checks.why: Accepting the Messenger ﷺ means accepting everything he brought, including the angels, the books and the Last Day.

checks.q: What does al-Sanusi advise about the Shahadah?
checks.a: Say it often, knowing its meaning
w: Say it once in your life
checks.why: He closes by urging the believer to say it often while aware of what it means.

lessons.title: What a believer believes
lessons.about: The articles of faith, what faith is, and love of the Companions.

cards.x: A believer believes in Allah, His angels, His books, His Messengers, the Last Day, and that good and bad are by Allah's decree.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on faith and the Companions

cards.x: Faith (iman) is affirming with the tongue and believing with the heart everything the Prophet ﷺ brought from Allah.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on faith and the Companions

cards.x: We love the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. We do not go to excess in loving any one of them, and we do not disown any of them. We mention them only with good.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on faith and the Companions

checks.q: According to al-Tahawi, faith is…
checks.a: Affirming with the tongue and believing with the heart
w: Only believing, with no need to say it
Only saying it with the tongue
checks.why: Al-Tahawi defines faith as affirming with the tongue and believing with the heart what the Prophet ﷺ brought.
checks.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on faith and the Companions

checks.q: Which is one of the articles of faith?
checks.a: Belief in Allah's decree, the good and the bad
w: Belief that the stars decide events
Belief that some saints are prophets
checks.why: Belief in Allah's decree, the good and the bad, is one of the articles of faith, with Allah, His angels, books, Messengers and the Last Day.
checks.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on faith and the Companions

checks.q: How do we speak of the Companions?
checks.a: Only with good, without going to excess about any of them
w: We praise some and disown others
checks.why: We love all the Companions, go to excess with none of them, disown none of them, and mention them only with good.
checks.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on faith and the Companions

lessons.title: The grave and the Last Day
lessons.about: What al-Tahawi tells us to believe about what comes after death.

cards.x: We believe in the punishment of the grave for those who deserve it, and in the questioning by Munkar and Nakir about one's Lord, religion and Prophet. The grave is a garden of Paradise or a pit of the Fire.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on the hereafter

cards.x: We believe in the resurrection, the recompense of deeds on the Day of Judgement, the presenting of records, the reckoning, the reading of the book, the reward and punishment, the Bridge and the Scales.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on the hereafter

cards.x: The Pool (hawd) with which Allah honoured the Prophet ﷺ, to quench his Ummah, is true. The intercession he has stored for them is true.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, the Pool and the intercession

cards.x: Paradise and the Fire are created. They will never end and never perish.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on Paradise and the Fire

checks.q: Who questions a person in the grave?
checks.why: Al-Tahawi: we believe in the questioning of Munkar and Nakir about one's Lord, religion and Prophet.

checks.q: What does al-Tahawi say about Paradise and the Fire?
checks.a: They are created and will never end
w: They will be created on the Last Day
They end after a long time
checks.why: They are already created, and they never end or perish.

checks.q: The Pool (hawd) is…
checks.a: True: Allah honoured the Prophet ﷺ with it for his Ummah
checks.why: Al-Tahawi affirms the Pool as true, an honour for the Prophet ﷺ to quench his Ummah.

lessons.title: Allah's decree (qadr)
lessons.about: Everything happens by His knowledge and will.

cards.x: Allah knew everything before creating it, and decreed it. Nothing happens in His kingdom except what He wills.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on decree

cards.x: The decree is Allah's secret in His creation. No angel near to Him nor Prophet sent has been shown it. Looking too deeply into it leads to ruin.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on decree

cards.x: Our actions are created by Allah and earned (kasb) by us. So we act, we take responsibility, and we trust Him.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on decree

checks.q: What happens in Allah's kingdom?
checks.why: Al-Tahawi: nothing happens except what He wills.

checks.q: What does al-Tahawi say about looking deeply into decree?
checks.a: It is Allah's secret; delving into it leads to ruin
w: Everyone must study it in detail
Only Prophets may ask about it
checks.why: The decree is Allah's secret in His creation; no one has been shown it.

checks.q: Our actions are…
checks.a: Created by Allah and earned by us
w: Forced on us with no choice
checks.why: They are Allah's creation and our earning (kasb), so we are responsible for them.

lessons.title: Prophets, saints and wonders
lessons.about: The rank of the awliya' and their karamat.

cards.x: We do not prefer any wali to any Prophet عليهم السلام. One Prophet is better than all the awliya' together.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, Prophets and awliya'

cards.x: We believe in the wonders (karamat) of the awliya' that are reported by trustworthy narrators.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, Prophets and awliya'

cards.x: The believers are all friends (awliya') of the Most Merciful. The most honoured of them with Allah are the most obedient and the best followers of the Qur'an.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on faith

checks.q: Can a wali be better than a Prophet?
checks.a: No, one Prophet is better than all the awliya'
checks.why: Al-Tahawi: one Prophet is better than all the awliya' together.

checks.q: The karamat of the awliya' are…
checks.a: True, when reported by trustworthy narrators
checks.why: We believe in their wonders, as reported by trustworthy narrators.

checks.q: Who is most honoured with Allah?
checks.a: The most obedient and best follower of the Qur'an
w: The one with the most wonders
The one from the best family
checks.why: Al-Tahawi ties honour with Allah to obedience and following the Qur'an.

title: Fiqh
sub: Purification, prayer, fasting and zakat, in the Hanafi school

lessons.title: Foundations: fard, wajib and sunnah
lessons.about: The school we follow and the words fiqh uses.

cards.x: This course follows the Hanafi school of Imam Abu Hanifah al-Nu'man رحمه الله, through Nur al-Idah of Imam al-Shurunbulali رحمه الله and Mukhtasar al-Quduri of Imam al-Quduri رحمه الله.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah; Mukhtasar al-Quduri

cards.x: Fard is what is established by a definitive proof with no doubt in it. You must act on it and believe in it.
cards.src: Usul al-Shashi, on fard and wajib

cards.x: Wajib is established by a proof with some doubt in it. It is like fard in action, so you may not leave it, but you are not required to believe in it with certainty as you do with fard.
cards.src: Usul al-Shashi, on fard and wajib

checks.q: Fard is established by…
checks.a: A definitive proof with no doubt in it
checks.why: Al-Shashi: fard is what is established by a definitive proof with no doubt in it.

checks.q: Can you leave a wajib act?
checks.a: No, it is like fard in action
checks.why: Wajib is like fard in action: you may not leave it.

checks.q: How is wajib different from fard?
checks.a: You are not required to believe in it with certainty
w: It is more important than fard
checks.why: Wajib is fard in action but not in belief, because its proof carries some doubt.

lessons.title: Water you can use
lessons.about: Which water you may use to purify yourself, and which you may not.

cards.x: You may purify yourself with seven kinds of water: rain, sea, river, well, melted snow, melted hail and spring water.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the waters that may be used

cards.x: If something pure is mixed with water and the water is still called water, you may use it. If it has become something else, like juice or soup, you may not.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the waters that may be used

cards.x: Water that has already been used for wudu or ghusl is pure, but you cannot purify yourself with it again.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the waters that may be used

checks.q: Which water can be used for wudu?
checks.why: Rain water is one of the seven waters Nur al-Idah lists: rain, sea, river, well, snow, hail and spring.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the waters that may be used

checks.q: Can you make wudu with water used for someone's ghusl?
checks.a: No: it is pure but does not purify
checks.why: Water already used for wudu or ghusl is pure, but it cannot purify you a second time.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the waters that may be used

checks.q: How many kinds of water does Nur al-Idah list for purification?
checks.why: Nur al-Idah lists seven kinds of water you may purify yourself with.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the waters that may be used

lessons.title: The four obligations of wudu
lessons.about: The four things without which wudu is not valid.

cards.x: Wash the whole face: from the top of the forehead to under the chin, and from one earlobe to the other.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the obligations of wudu

cards.x: Wash both hands and arms, including the elbows.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the obligations of wudu

cards.x: Wipe at least a quarter of the head with a wet hand.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the obligations of wudu

cards.x: Wash both feet, including the ankles. If any of these four is missed, the wudu is not valid.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the obligations of wudu

checks.q: How much of the head must be wiped in wudu?
checks.why: Wiping a quarter of the head is the obligation. Wiping all of it once is sunnah.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the obligations of wudu

checks.q: How far must the arms be washed?
checks.why: The arms are washed up to and including the elbows.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the obligations of wudu

checks.q: Which of these is one of the four obligations of wudu?
checks.a: Washing the feet including the ankles
checks.why: The four obligations are the face, the arms with the elbows, a quarter of the head, and the feet with the ankles.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the obligations of wudu

lessons.title: The sunnahs of wudu
lessons.about: How to make your wudu complete by following the sunnah.

cards.x: Have the intention, say bismillah, wash the hands to the wrists and use the siwak (even a finger if you have no siwak).
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the sunnahs of wudu

cards.x: Rinse the mouth three times and sniff water into the nose three times.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the sunnahs of wudu

cards.x: Wash each part three times, wipe the whole head once and the ears, run water between the fingers and toes, start with the right, follow the order Allah mentions, and keep going without long breaks.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the sunnahs of wudu

checks.q: In the Hanafi school, rinsing the mouth in wudu is…
checks.why: In the Hanafi school, rinsing the mouth is a sunnah of wudu (in ghusl it is fard).
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the sunnahs of wudu

checks.q: How many times is each part washed according to the sunnah?
checks.why: The sunnah is to wash each part three times. Once is enough for validity.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the sunnahs of wudu

checks.q: Which is a sunnah of wudu?
w: Wiping the neck with the back of the hand only
checks.why: Starting with the right is one of the sunnahs of wudu.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the sunnahs of wudu

lessons.title: What breaks wudu
lessons.about: What breaks wudu in the Hanafi school, and what does not.

cards.x: Anything that comes out of the front or back passage, flowing blood or pus, and vomit that fills the mouth all break wudu.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks wudu, and what does not

cards.x: Sleeping without being seated firmly on the ground breaks it, as do fainting, insanity and drunkenness.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks wudu, and what does not

cards.x: Laughing out loud in a prayer with bowing and prostration breaks both the prayer and the wudu, for a sane, awake adult.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks wudu, and what does not

cards.x: Touching your private part, touching a woman, blood that does not flow, vomit that does not fill the mouth, and dozing while sitting firmly do not break wudu.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks wudu, and what does not

checks.q: Which breaks wudu in the Hanafi school?
w: A spot of blood that does not flow
checks.why: Blood that flows from the body breaks wudu. Blood that does not flow does not.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks wudu, and what does not

checks.q: Which kind of sleep breaks wudu?
checks.a: Sleep without being seated firmly on the ground
w: Sleeping in the sunnah way in prostration
A moment of drowsiness while sitting
checks.why: Sleep breaks wudu when you are not seated firmly on the ground. Dozing while seated firmly does not.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks wudu, and what does not

checks.q: Laughing out loud during the prayer…
checks.a: Breaks both the prayer and the wudu
checks.why: Laughing out loud in a prayer with ruku' and sujud breaks both the prayer and the wudu.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks wudu, and what does not

lessons.title: Ghusl: the full bath
lessons.about: When ghusl becomes fard and how to do it properly.

title: Dealing with Doubts

lessons.about: What the Prophet ﷺ said to Companions troubled by thoughts.

cards.src: Hadith, Sahih Muslim, Book of Faith

cards.x: The Prophet ﷺ said Shaytan comes and asks: who created this, who created that, until he asks who created your Lord. When that happens, seek refuge in Allah and stop.
cards.src: Hadith, al-Bukhari and Muslim

cards.src: Hadith, Sahih Muslim, Book of Faith
